title: Scarborough Marsh Audubon Center
specs: State's largest salt marsh with tidal marsh, salt creeks, freshwater marsh, and uplands
Important habitat for waterfowl, egrets, herons, Glossy Ibis, shorebirds, grassland songbirds, birds of prey, muskrat, mink, otter, and deer
Boating is tide dependent; do not go out one hour before or after low tide
blurb: The center offers naturalist-guided and self-guided tours, exhibits, a nature trail, canoe/kayak rentals, and a nature store. Visitors can explore tidal marsh, salt creeks, freshwater marsh, and uplands. The marsh is important for wildlife as a resting, breeding, and feeding ground.
extraNote: Walk-in service is on a first come, first served basis · June 15 through September 7, 2026
